GoF calibration

Source: vignettes/articles/gof-calibration.Rmd
gof-calibration.Rmd

Goodness-of-fit calibration

The martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family (gof_univariate(), gof_global(), gof_auxiliary(), martingale_residuals()) reports p-values against an analytic null. This article measures the type-I error of gof_univariate() under correct specification: simulate from a model, fit the same model, and collect the p-values. For a calibrated test they are Uniform(0, 1), so the rejection rate at level α equals α.

Settings. A 20-actor one-mode network, the Gillespie simulator, 1,500 events, one control per case (the design the GoF uses), and 600 replicates per cell. With 600 replicates the Monte Carlo standard error of a rejection rate near 0.05 is about 0.009.

library(amorem)
library(parallel)
actors <- paste0("a", 1:20)

# one replicate under correct specification: simulate with a known effect,
# fit the same linear model, return the gof_univariate p-value
gof_rep <- function(i, beta, stat, half_life = NULL) {
  set.seed(70000L + i)
  ev <- simulate_relational_events(
    n_events = 1500, senders = actors, receivers = actors,
    endogenous_stats = stat, endogenous_effects = setNames(beta, stat),
    half_life = half_life, method = "gillespie")
  gof_univariate(ev, model = setNames("linear", stat), covariate = stat,
                 half_life = half_life, seed = 90000L + i)$p_value
}

cells <- list(
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.0),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.1),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.2),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.3),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_count", beta = 0.5),
  list(stat = "recency", beta = 0.2),
  list(stat = "reciprocity_exp_decay", beta = 0.2, half_life = 5))
p <- lapply(cells, function(g) unlist(mclapply(1:600, gof_rep, beta = g$beta,
          stat = g$stat, half_life = g$half_life, mc.cores = 8)))

The p-values from that run (amorem 1.1.0) are stored with this article, and the table and figure below are computed from them.

res <- readRDS("data/gof-calibration.rds")
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(res, list(res$stat, res$beta), drop = TRUE),
  function(d) data.frame(
    statistic     = d$stat[1],
    true_beta     = d$beta[1],
    replicates    = sum(!is.na(d$p_value)),
    reject_05     = mean(d$p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    reject_10     = mean(d$p_value < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
    ks_uniformity = suppressWarnings(stats::ks.test(stats::na.omit(d$p_value),
                                                    "punif")$p.value))))
tab <- tab[order(tab$statistic != "reciprocity_count", tab$statistic, tab$true_beta), ]
rownames(tab) <- NULL
knitr::kable(tab, digits = c(0, 1, 0, 3, 3, 4))
statistic true_beta replicates reject_05 reject_10 ks_uniformity
reciprocity_count 0.0 600 0.050 0.083 0.6699
reciprocity_count 0.1 600 0.045 0.077 0.0018
reciprocity_count 0.2 600 0.037 0.080 0.0673
reciprocity_count 0.3 600 0.047 0.113 0.4504
reciprocity_count 0.5 600 0.038 0.072 0.0000
recency 0.2 600 0.078 0.152 0.0006
reciprocity_exp_decay 0.2 600 0.048 0.097 0.5429 
show <- list(c("reciprocity_count", 0.2), c("reciprocity_exp_decay", 0.2),
             c("recency", 0.2))
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, 1))
for (s in show) {
  pv <- sort(res$p_value[res$stat == s[1] & res$beta == as.numeric(s[2])])
  plot(pv, seq_along(pv) / length(pv), type = "s", lwd = 2, col = "#1f5fb4",
       xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "p-value", ylab = "empirical CDF",
       main = sprintf("%s, beta = %s", s[1], s[2]), cex.main = 0.9)
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
}

par(op)

Reading the results

  • Count statistic. For reciprocity_count the rejection rate at the 5% level ranges from 0.037 to 0.050 across true effects from 0 to 0.5, at most 1.5 Monte Carlo standard errors (0.009) from 0.05. The p-value distribution is not exactly uniform in every cell: the uniformity test gives p = 0.0018 at β = 0.1 and p = 7.1e-06 at β = 0.5, while the rejection rate at 5% stays at nominal.
  • Decayed statistic. reciprocity_exp_decay rejects at 0.048 (uniformity p = 0.543).
  • Recency. recency rejects at 0.078, which is 3.2 Monte Carlo standard errors above 0.05 (uniformity p = 5.9e-04).

Guidance

  • For count and decayed statistics, the p-values can be used at the 5% level in settings like these.
  • For recency, the test rejects a correct model more often than the nominal level (0.078 at 5%); read its p-value together with the cumulative residual process and martingale_residuals().
  • These cells cover one network size, one sample size and one control per case. The rejection rate as the number of controls grows has not been measured.

See the Estimation guide for the GoF API and Validation experiments for the recovery and parity studies (E1–E7).
